description:
An access token of a `ForgejoUser` (typically a bot), issued through the
admin API (Forgejo v16+) and written to `secretTargets` as
`FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_USERNAME` and `FORGEJO_URL`.

Token values can't be read back: a lost target, a new
`forgejo.weebo.io/rotate-secret` nonce or an elapsed `rotationPeriod`
issues a new token. The new token is issued and written to every target
before the old one is revoked; as names are unique per user, a rotated
token alternates between `name` and `name-next`.

deletionPolicy.description: What happens to the Forgejo object when its CR is deleted.

instanceRef.description:
The `ForgejoInstance` or `ForgejoLocalInstance` this object lives
on. Unset: the cluster's only `ForgejoInstance`, else the only
`ForgejoLocalInstance` of this namespace.

kind.description: The kind of instance a reference designates.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: namespace only applies to kind LocalInstance

name.description:
Token name, unique per user. Defaults to `<namespace>-<cr name>`.
A token of that name the user already has, or another CR issues, is
never revoked: the CR fails (`ForgejoObjectAlreadyExists`,
`RemoteObjectClaimed`). Rotation alternates with `<name>-next`.

repositoryRefs.description:
Restrict the token to these `ForgejoRepository`s (same namespace).
Forgejo then only accepts the `read:`/`write:` `issue` and
`repository` scopes. Same disruptive-update rule as `scopes`.

items.description:
Reference to another CR of this operator, by `metadata.name`. Always a
CR, never a raw remote name: a cluster-scoped target is looked up
cluster-wide, a namespaced one in the referencing CR's own namespace only.

rotationPeriod.description:
Issue a new token once the current one is this old — a Go duration
such as `720h`.

scopes.description:
`all`, or `read:`/`write:` + `activitypub`, `admin`, `issue`,
`misc`, `notification`, `organization`, `package`, `repository`,
`user`. Changing scopes issues a new token, which needs the
`forgejo.weebo.io/allow-disruptive-update: "true"` annotation.

secretTargets.description:
Defaults to one target named after the CR, in its namespace, on the
instance's default `secretStore` backend.

items.description:
Where an emitted secret (generated password or key, OAuth2 credentials,
access token) is written. A CR may list several targets — the same
value is fanned out to each.

backend.description:
`kubernetes` (default) or `vault`. A Vault target reuses the Vault
connection (address, mount, auth) the instance configures, which it
must then do.

name.description:
Kubernetes: the `Secret` name. Vault: names the default path
`<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/<name>` when `path` is unset.

namespace.description:
Kubernetes `Secret` namespace (Vault: the namespace segment of the
default path). Defaults to the CR's own namespace; required on
cluster-scoped CRs. A namespaced CR may only name its own namespace.

path.description:
Vault only: explicit KV v2 path under the instance's mount. It must
stay under `<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/` (this object's namespace, or
the target's on a cluster-scoped object), unless the instance's
`pathGrants` open it to this object.

userRef.description: The user the token belongs to.

namespace.description: Namespace of the CR; defaults to this object's own.

remoteName.description:
Forgejo name of an object no CR manages (a user's login, an
organization's or team's name).

x-kubernetes-validations.message: set exactly one of name and remoteName
